headline: Where the Desert Drops Into the Sea
dek: Five coastlines that barely look real
editorial_intent: Deliver five vivid and authentic globally diverse examples of deserts or dry dune landscapes literally reaching saltwater, with precise site names for visitors to discover.
reader_scenario: A reader wants unusual sea landscapes and striking photographic trip inspiration beyond familiar blue-water beaches.
share_reason: This five-country carousel sparks the wait-where-is-that reaction with the rare sight of deserts falling directly into the sea, with photographs tied to real named destinations.
slide_count_rationale: 7 distinct authentic original photographs, 1 scenic branded final slide created from the same licensed images. Extra views chosen for different scenes and reader value.
caption:
A desert doesn't always end at an oasis. Sometimes it runs straight into the sea. 🌊🏜️

📍 Sandwich Harbour, Namibia — sweeping Namib dunes meet the Atlantic.
📍 Paracas, Peru — arid cliffs drop towards the Pacific.
📍 Khor Al Adaid, Qatar — pale dunes line a vast tidal inland sea.
📍 Dune du Pilat, France — Europe's tallest sand dune rises beside the ocean.
📍 Cape Peron, Western Australia — red coastal land meets Shark Bay's blue waters.

Which coastline would you explore first?

Photos: NIR HIMI, Kimberly Genest, World Thing & Dylan Shaw, Slim MARS / Unsplash; Kevin Gong / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 (cropped and text overlaid): https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/.
